judge.reason: The assistant refused to guess competitors, explained why in one clear sentence (a wrong set yields a confident but useless comparison), named no competitors of its own, and offered both to skip compare in favor of a single-site assessment and to accept user-supplied URLs.

reply:
I can't pick the competitors for this. The compare mode has one rule I won't bend: **competitors come from you, never from me**.

Here's why. If I guess, the result looks exactly as confident as one built on the right set. The matrix would say "you trail X on pricing clarity" with evidence from both sides, and nothing in it would show that X was my guess and not your real rival. Only you know whether the site you're worried about is the obvious one or one nobody would think to name. For the same reason I won't list candidates for you to approve.

I also checked for a saved target for Nimbus Notes that might already list competitors. There isn't one, so I have no set to fall back on.

**What I need:** 1–3 competitor URLs. Your sales or support team can often tell you who prospects mention, or who you lose deals to.

**If you don't have any, that's a fine answer.** The comparison just can't run without them. Instead I can do a single-site assessment of https://example-nimbus-notes.test with `/understudy:run`, looking at clarity, trust and conversion. You can add a comparison later once you know who to compare against.

Once you send URLs, I'll confirm the scope and time with you before starting. With three sites it's roughly 1h 50m, because every site gets the same capture and scoring. Only the public, logged-out pages get compared. I won't create an account, fill in a form or send a message on any competitor's site.
